solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Wild parties interrupted by a problem for host

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are broken into by the single letter a, which sits within them
wild parties are out of control, so the letters of the word parties run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A host's evening ruined by riotous parties gatecrashed by trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The host is a biological host, not a party-giver: 'Wild' rearranges PARTIES into PARSITE, and 'interrupted by' sets A inside it after PAR.
explanation.definitionFit: An organism living off another creature is a burden and threat to the animal or plant that harbours it.

clue.text: Stop fighting if surrounded by fleet

indicators.note: the word if is enclosed by the word for fast

parts.note: fleet means fast, which is pacy

explanation.surface: A demand for a ceasefire, conditional on being encircled by a navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fleet' looks like a navy but is the adjective meaning quick.
explanation.definitionFit: To calm others and end hostilities is to bring peace, the sense of the verb here.

clue.text: Platforms in section of ramparts originally set up

indicators.note: set up says the hidden letters are read backwards
a section of the words means a stretch of letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Raised stages built into part of the old ramparts at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'in section' in the definition, but 'in section of' signals the hidden stretch ARTSOR, which 'set up' reverses; the definition is 'Platforms' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Speakers' daises, a plural of the Latin word for a raised speaking platform.

clue.text: Bullet has done damage, less than fatal

indicators.note: something damaged is broken up, so the letters of the two words are reshaped

explanation.surface: A gunshot wound that hurt but did not kill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' belongs in the fodder, so 'done damage' alone signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Something insufficient to cause death, such as a dose just below the lethal level, is described this way.

clue.text: Find what's wrong with foreign money — get out time after time

indicators.note: after places the earlier pieces behind this second abbreviation

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time, used again
the rouble is the Russian currency
shoo is said to drive someone or something away

explanation.surface: Fixing a problem with a foreign currency, telling someone to leave again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time after time' is not repetition here: one T ends the answer, and 'after' places that whole run behind a second T at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: To diagnose and fix faults in a system or machine is to trace and solve its problems.

clue.text: It's not about you, in French dialect

indicators.note: about means going around, so the French negative wraps the French pronoun

parts.note: pas is the French word for not, the 'in French' covering both pieces
toi is the familiar French word for you

explanation.surface: A remark that this French speech isn't aimed at you personally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in French' governs both pieces: PAS (not) goes 'about' TOI (you).
explanation.definitionFit: A regional form of speech, especially a rural or nonstandard variety of French, is called a patois.

clue.text: As Cecily Cardew was for Oscar, say

definitions.meaning: Cecily is Jack Worthing's ward in Wilde's The Importance of Being Earnest, so she was a ward
an Oscar is an example of a prize given by the film academy

explanation.surface: What Wilde's character Cecily Cardew meant to her author Oscar.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first part as two words, A WARD; the Oscar is the film prize, not Wilde.
explanation.definitionFit: An Academy statuette is one instance of a prize presented for achievement.

clue.text: Series of deliveries that is taken in car, in summary

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled

indicators.note: the abbreviation for that is goes inside the car's initials

parts.note: VW is a Volkswagen car
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A cricket over watched while sitting in a car, summarised.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is cricket's run of six balls from one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: A general survey of a subject giving its main points is a broad outline of it.

clue.text: Author poking fun at flower-girl in street

indicators.note: the two pieces are placed within the street abbreviation

parts.note: Iris is both a flower and a girl's name

explanation.surface: A writer mocking a girl selling flowers in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' leaves 'poking fun' and joins the wordplay; 'flower-girl' is one piece, IRIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer who ridicules people or institutions through mockery and irony is this kind of author.

clue.text: Record of work doctor compiled for consultant

definitions.text: Record of work doctor compiled for consultant

parts.words: Record of work doctor compiled for consultant
parts.note: the doctor is Dr Watson and the consulting detective is Sherlock Holmes; Conan Doyle's last Holmes collection bears this title

explanation.surface: A medical registrar's notes of cases put together for a hospital specialist.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests hospital medicine, but Holmes called himself a consulting detective, and Watson wrote up his cases; The Case-Book of Sherlock Holmes was the final volume.
explanation.definitionFit: A volume recording professional cases, and the title of a book of detective stories narrated by Watson.

clue.text: Scouts look for this article left in part of camp

indicators.note: the article and the abbreviation are placed within the camp shelter

parts.note: a tent is one unit of a campsite
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Boy Scouts pitching camp and hunting for a lost item left in a tent.
explanation.walkthrough: The scouts are talent scouts looking for promising performers, not Boy Scouts, though the camp imagery pushes that way.
explanation.definitionFit: Talent scouts search for people with natural ability or gifts, which is what they hope to discover.

clue.text: Change to club's price that could be the government's business

indicators.note: the letters of these words are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A club hiking its fees, which the state might count as its affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' belongs in the fodder with CLUBS PRICE.
explanation.definitionFit: The part of the economy run by the state, its services and enterprises, is official business.

clue.text: Steadily proceed to make money illegally

definitions.meaning: to move forward gradually and steadily

explanation.surface: Advice to plod onward towards earning cash through crime.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to advance steadily and to produce a fake copy, such as counterfeit currency.

clue.text: Required to keep out of trouble, that's clear

definitions.text: Required to keep out of trouble
definitions.meaning: a court can order an offender to keep the peace, putting them under a legal obligation
leapt over an obstacle, so cleared it

explanation.surface: A probation order with a note that the matter is now settled.
explanation.walkthrough: In British courts a person 'bound over' must keep the peace for a set period or forfeit money.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both the legal order to behave and a description of a jump that cleared something.

clue.text: Young women whose hips arouse sports fans?

definitions.text: Young women whose hips arouse sports fans?

parts.words: Young women whose hips arouse sports fans?
parts.note: the hips are the 'hip, hip' of 'hip, hip, hurrah', shouted to rouse a crowd

explanation.surface: A leering remark about young women's figures exciting a stadium crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hips' means the shouts 'hip, hip, hooray', and 'arouse' means stir to cheer, not titillate.
explanation.definitionFit: Squad members leading crowd chants at games stir supporters into shouting their encouragement.

clue.text: Revision in note people twice produced on time

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the time abbreviation follows

parts.note: A is a note of the musical scale
men means people
the note and people come again: D, another note, then MEN

explanation.surface: A redrafting in a memo that people produced twice over in good time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note people twice' gives a note plus MEN two times, with different notes: A MEN and D MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An alteration made to a text or law is a correction or change to it.

clue.text: Something French like to eat — not fast food

definitions.text: Something French like to eat — not fast food

parts.words: Something French like to eat — not fast food
parts.note: a French delicacy that is a snail, a famously slow creature

explanation.surface: A dish the French enjoy that is not a quick takeaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not fast food' is both a gourmet dish and a slow creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Snails cooked in garlic butter are a classic French delicacy, and snails crawl slowly.

clue.text: Occasions for retirement in base daily

parts.note: a bed is a base, as in a riverbed or flowerbed
The Times is a daily newspaper

explanation.surface: When to retire from work, as read in a basic daily paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' is going to bed, not leaving work.
explanation.definitionFit: The hours when one goes to sleep are the moments of retiring for the night.

clue.text: Turn attack on king and queen that reveals character flaws

parts.note: a spell is a turn or stint, as in 'a spell on duty'
in chess, check is an attack on the king
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A chess move against king and queen exposing a player's weaknesses of character.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'character' is a printed letter, not a personality.
explanation.definitionFit: Software that flags typing mistakes exposes faults in individual letters, which are characters in the typographic sense.

clue.text: Fate or destiny hard to see in firm

indicators.note: the pieces are placed so they can be seen inside the company abbreviation

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
one's lot is one's destiny
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Whether a company's fortune is hard to foresee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fate' is a proper noun: Clotho is one of the three Fates of Greek myth, who spins the thread of life.
explanation.definitionFit: Of the three Greek goddesses controlling human destiny, she is the one spinning life's thread.

clue.text: To some extent, relatives manage fine

parts.note: kin are one's relatives
to do is to manage, as in 'we'll do'
F is the pencil abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: Family members cope reasonably well, more or less.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal phrase means somewhat or rather, softening a statement to a partial degree.

clue.text: Vegetable that's all right in acre hit disastrously

indicators.note: the abbreviation for all right is placed within the rearranged letters
a disaster leaves things in a mess, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written, for rearranging
OK means all right

explanation.surface: A field crop that survived when an acre was hit by catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disastrously' scrambles the seven letters of 'acre hit' into ARTICHE, and 'in' sets the letters for all right just before its final E.
explanation.definitionFit: The globe kind is a thistle-like plant whose flower head is eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Food that's hot or cold, we hear, in this country

indicators.note: the spoken words give a name spelt differently

parts.note: chilli is a hot pepper, and chilly, cold, sounds the same

explanation.surface: A dish served hot or cold in a certain nation.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'hot' food, chilli, and 'cold', chilly, sound like the country.
explanation.definitionFit: The long thin South American republic along the Pacific coast is the nation referred to.

clue.text: Capital at one time husband invested in food store

indicators.note: invested means installed, so the abbreviation is set inside the shop name

parts.note: a deli, delicatessen, sells prepared foods

explanation.surface: Money once put by a married man into a grocery business.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Delhi was the Mughal capital; the modern capital of India is New Delhi, hence 'at one time'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian city served as an imperial seat of government in earlier centuries, before its new district took over.

clue.text: Opening of a sort, in part of Africa — time for a change, finally

indicators.note: one letter is put in place of another, here the clock abbreviation in place of the article
the swap happens at the very end of the country's name

parts.note: Gambia is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: An African venture beginning, with a note that it is time things changed.
explanation.walkthrough: GAMBIA has two A's; 'finally' says the last one is replaced by T.
explanation.definitionFit: A chess opening in which a pawn or piece is sacrificed is a particular kind of opening move.

clue.text: A temperature checked and confirmed in trial

parts.note: tested means examined or checked

explanation.surface: A patient's temperature measured and verified during a clinical trial.
explanation.definitionFit: Evidence borne out in court by a witness's sworn statement is said to be vouched for formally.

clue.text: Decisively raised a bit of money before game

definitions.text: Decisively raised a bit of money before game

parts.words: Decisively raised a bit of money before game
parts.note: a coin is flipped into the air before a match to decide which side starts

explanation.surface: Someone raising a little cash ahead of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised a bit of money' looks like fundraising; it means flipping a coin for the start of a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Flipping a coin up to settle choice of ends or first innings is the usual pre-match ritual.

clue.text: Cancel ceremony, we hear, not taking place

indicators.note: the word for ceremony is spoken, giving a word sounding the same but spelt differently

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony
an event that is off has been called off

explanation.surface: A ceremony that has been called off, as the rumour has it.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss a debt or loss as unrecoverable is to annul it in the accounts.
